# PR #12668 retrospective

## What worked

Fresh native Opus 5.5 High and Sol Xhigh sessions received equivalent neutral scope. Security triage preceded reviewer reset and code execution. Both finals were saved before either was read. Independent source review and narrowly corrected runtime evidence converged without sharing conclusions. A no-write selector stub was sufficient for the important discovery/exit question; actual GUI resources were unnecessary. -H matches the advertised starting-point behavior.

## Deviations and remediation

Preserve all native history and fixture revisions. Opus combined 80 policy lines in one response despite the upfront 60-line aggregate bound; no oversized native-result persistence notice was reported. Original drivers read mountinfo, used unguarded real-selector mktemp/rm operations and delayed expected-status gates. Coordinator discovered these in source audit, withdrew broad runtime totals and requested an explicit audit addendum and a narrow corrected fixture. The mountinfo prohibition had been present in coordinator guidance but not repeated verbatim in the initial reviewer dispatch; this assignment's audit correction now passes it explicitly. Corrected rev5 avoids mount discovery and real selector mutation, and gates status before result parsing. It still cannot establish per-internal-temp-path preguards for Bash here-strings or possible sort spill, so report that limit and never claim complete guard coverage. No additional experiments are warranted for this conclusion.

## Carry-forward instruction correction

For this assignment and future launch templates: explicitly prohibit mountinfo discovery in the reviewer dispatch; keep policy reads <=60 aggregate lines per response. Before running even a tiny shell fixture, inventory interpreter here-string backing files, utility spill paths, caller redirections and automatic cleanup, not only explicit stub writes. Prefer no-write stubs when native selector behavior is not material. Require expected child status before reading or summarizing payloads. Root redirection and empty-directory postconditions are containment, not pre-write target assertions. Never claim whole-run compliance from a seal or end marker. Preserve failed init/provenance cases separately. Keep audit remediation separate from substantive review and do not silently rewrite final reports.

## Tooling

No confirmed new Omadev/review.py bug. Uppercase source-label rejection and blob/commit constant mix-up were fixture setup mistakes. No desktop used or requested. No model fallback or quota exhaustion occurred. Process-only startup memory is a disclosed independence limit; no substantive prior-PR conclusions were loaded or shared according to the native reviewer records.

## Cleanup

Runtime subprocesses completed without timeouts and private namespaces ended. Source, raw evidence, native history and reviewer panes remain preserved. Reviewer agents are stopped only by their coordinator via recorded owned pane identities. The outer assistant alone handles any publication and subsequent team reset.
comment:
**Verified:** Symlinked directory roots now contribute matching files to the picker. One edge-case regression remains: a nested symlink loop can turn a returned selection into failure.

### Nested symlink loops discard successful selections

In [`bin/omarchy-menu-file`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/548effcc231c2c50b8f66a15dbacf4e1c7ceee07/bin/omarchy-menu-file#L47-L49), `-L` follows interior links too, not just the starting directories. A synthetic tree demonstrates the difference:

```text
Pictures/
  x.jpg
  sub/y.png
  sub/loop -> Pictures/   (link back to the root)
```

With a selector stub returning `x.jpg`:

| File discovery | Selection returned | Command exit |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline `find` | `x.jpg` | 0 |
| PR `find -L` | `x.jpg` | 1 |
| Diagnostic `find -H` | `x.jpg` | 0 |

`find -L` reports a filesystem loop and exits 1. Its diagnostic is suppressed, but `pipefail` propagates that failure after selection.

**Impact:** `omarchy-transcode` assigns this result under `set -e`, so it aborts instead of continuing after a pick. This consequence follows from caller source inspection; the real UI was not exercised.

**Suggested change:** Use `find -H` to follow command-line directory links without traversing interior links. The diagnostic variant also retained the symlink-root fix in the synthetic positive control.

**Pre-existing limitation:** #12665 additionally reports an argument-size failure for a large library. The unchanged selector still passes the entire JSON option list as one argument. This PR fixes discovery, not that size limit; consider tracking that part separately rather than treating the whole issue as resolved. This is a source-based scope note, not a new regression or reproduction of the reporter's dataset.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Head `548effcc231c2c50b8f66a15dbacf4e1c7ceee07`; isolated synthetic trees with the real file-discovery script and a selector stub, plus source/documentation inspection. No real menu, transcoding, or user media library was tested.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium inspected source and adjudicated evidence after independent Opus 5.5 High technical review with targeted tests and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh source/documentation review.
